Hầu hết các ví tạo ra **cụm từ khôi phục** (seed phrase, còn gọi là recovery phrase hoặc mnemonic), thường là 12 hoặc 24 từ phổ biến theo thứ tự cụ thể. Cụm từ này là bản sao lưu khóa riêng tư của bạn mà con người có thể đọc được. Viết ra giấy, cất giữ an toàn ngoại tuyến và không bao giờ chụp ảnh hoặc lưu trữ kỹ thuật số. Bất kỳ ai có cụm từ khôi phục của bạn đều kiểm soát tiền của bạn.

Ví có nhiều loại. **Ví nóng** (hot wallet) luôn kết nối internet (ứng dụng di động, tiện ích mở rộng trình duyệt, phần mềm máy tính) và ưu tiên sự tiện lợi cho giao dịch thường xuyên. **Ví lạnh** (cold wallet) vẫn ngoại tuyến—thiết bị phần cứng như Ledger hoặc Trezor, hoặc thậm chí giấy in khóa của bạn. Lưu trữ lạnh giảm mạnh rủi ro bị hack và là tiêu chuẩn cho việc nắm giữ dài hạn. **Ví ký gửi** (custodial wallet) được cung cấp bởi sàn giao dịch: công ty giữ khóa riêng tư, bạn tin tưởng họ thực hiện việc rút tiền. **Ví không ký gửi** (non-custodial wallet) cho bạn toàn quyền kiểm soát và toàn bộ trách nhiệm. Mất cụm từ khôi phục với ví không ký gửi và tiền của bạn mất vĩnh viễn; không có công ty nào có thể khôi phục chúng.

sections.h: Sàn giao dịch và cách bạn giao dịch
p: **Sàn giao dịch tập trung** (CEX) như Binance, Remitano, hoặc VNDC là công ty giữ tiền điện tử của bạn trong ví ký gửi, ghép người mua với người bán và thường yêu cầu xác minh **Hiểu Biết Khách Hàng** (KYC)—tải lên CMND hoặc hộ chiếu và đôi khi bằng chứng địa chỉ. Quy định **Chống Rửa Tiền** (AML) khác nhau tùy theo khu vực pháp lý nhưng thường yêu cầu sàn giao dịch báo cáo các giao dịch lớn hoặc đáng ngờ. Các quy tắc này thay đổi thường xuyên và đây không phải là lời khuyên pháp lý; kiểm tra quy định hiện tại nơi bạn sống.

**Sàn giao dịch phi tập trung** (DEX) như Uniswap hoặc PancakeSwap chạy trên hợp đồng thông minh không có công ty ở giữa. Bạn kết nối ví không ký gửi của mình, giao dịch trực tiếp từ đó và trả **phí gas**—chi phí giao dịch mạng được trả cho người xác thực blockchain, thường bằng ETH trên Ethereum hoặc BNB trên BNB Smart Chain. Phí gas biến động theo tắc nghẽn mạng; đã dao động từ dưới 20.000 đồng đến hơn 2 triệu đồng trong thời gian cao điểm. DEX hiếm khi yêu cầu KYC, nhưng bạn chịu toàn bộ trách nhiệm về sai lầm: gửi tiền đến địa chỉ sai và không thể lấy lại.

Khi bạn đặt **lệnh thị trường** (market order), bạn mua hoặc bán ngay lập tức ở mức giá tốt nhất hiện có. **Lệnh giới hạn** (limit order) chỉ thực hiện ở mức giá bạn chọn hoặc tốt hơn, vì vậy bạn có thể chờ vô thời hạn nếu thị trường không bao giờ đạt đến đó. **Chênh lệch** (spread) là khoảng cách giữa mức chào mua cao nhất và mức chào bán thấp nhất; chênh lệch chặt chẽ hơn có nghĩa là chi phí thấp hơn. **Trượt giá** (slippage) xảy ra khi lệnh của bạn đủ lớn để di chuyển giá trong khi thực hiện, hoặc khi giá thay đổi giữa nhấp chuột và xác nhận. Trượt giá phổ biến hơn trên các cặp thanh khoản thấp và trên DEX trong thời kỳ biến động.

sections.h: Đòn bẩy, hợp đồng tương lai và thanh lý
p: **Giao dịch giao ngay** (spot trading) có nghĩa là mua tiền điện tử thực tế nằm trong ví của bạn. **Hợp đồng tương lai** (futures) là hợp đồng mua hoặc bán ở mức giá định sẵn vào một ngày trong tương lai, và bạn không sở hữu tài sản cơ bản—chỉ có hợp đồng. Hợp đồng tương lai cho phép bạn sử dụng **đòn bẩy** (leverage), vay bội số vốn của bạn: đòn bẩy 10x biến 2 triệu đồng thành 20 triệu đồng tiếp xúc thị trường. Lợi nhuận nhân lên, nhưng thua lỗ cũng vậy. Nếu thị trường di chuyển ngược bạn 10 phần trăm với đòn bẩy 10x, toàn bộ cược của bạn biến mất.

**Thanh lý** (liquidation) xảy ra khi thua lỗ ăn hết ký quỹ của bạn (tài sản thế chấp bạn đã ký gửi). Sàn giao dịch hoặc giao thức tự động đóng vị thế của bạn để ngăn bạn nợ nhiều hơn số bạn đã ký gửi. Giá thanh lý được tính tại thời điểm bạn mở vị thế có đòn bẩy; nếu Bitcoin giảm từ 1 tỷ đồng xuống 900 triệu đồng và giá thanh lý của bạn là 912 triệu đồng, bạn mất tất cả trước khi thị trường chạm 900 triệu đồng. Hợp đồng tương lai và đòn bẩy là công cụ rủi ro cao; nhiều nhà giao dịch lẻ thua lỗ, và đây không phải là lời khuyên đầu tư.

sections.h: Blockchain, layer và cầu nối
p: **Blockchain** là sổ cái giao dịch được chia sẻ, sao chép trên hàng nghìn máy tính (node). Mỗi khối giao dịch mới liên kết mật mã với khối trước đó, làm cho hồ sơ quá khứ gần như không thể thay đổi. **Bitcoin** chạy một blockchain; **Ethereum** chạy một blockchain khác. Mỗi cái xử lý giao dịch khác nhau và tính phí riêng.

Mạng **Layer 2** (L2) như Arbitrum, Optimism hoặc Polygon nằm trên chuỗi chính (Layer 1) và gộp nhiều giao dịch trước khi giải quyết chúng trên lớp cơ sở. L2 cắt giảm phí gas và tăng tốc xác nhận nhưng thêm sự đánh đổi về tin cậy hoặc độ phức tạp tùy thuộc vào thiết kế của chúng. **Cầu nối** (bridge) di chuyển tài sản giữa các blockchain—ví dụ, bọc Bitcoin để sử dụng trên Ethereum. Cầu nối dựa vào hợp đồng thông minh hoặc người giám sát; một số đã bị hack hàng trăm triệu đô la. Chỉ bắc cầu số tiền bạn có thể mất và nghiên cứu mô hình bảo mật của cầu trước khi sử dụng.

sections.h: Coin, token và vốn hóa thị trường
p: **Bitcoin** (BTC) là tiền điện tử đầu tiên; tất cả những cái khác là **altcoin**. Một số altcoin, như Ethereum (ETH), chạy blockchain riêng của họ. Những cái khác là **token** được xây dựng trên chuỗi hiện có bằng các tiêu chuẩn như ERC-20 (Ethereum) hoặc BEP-20 (BNB Chain). **Stablecoin** là token được thiết kế để giữ giá trị ổn định, thường được neo một-một với đô la Mỹ. USDT (Tether) và USDC (Circle) được hỗ trợ bởi dự trữ tiền mặt và trái phiếu, mặc dù chất lượng và kiểm toán dự trữ khác nhau. DAI là thuật toán, được hỗ trợ bởi tài sản thế chấp tiền điện tử bị khóa trong hợp đồng thông minh. Stablecoin đơn giản hóa giao dịch và lưu trữ giá trị, nhưng giám sát quy định đang tăng lên và một số đã mất neo trong khủng hoảng.

**Vốn hóa thị trường** (market cap) nhân giá hiện tại với nguồn cung lưu hành. Một coin có giá 50.000 đồng với 500 triệu token lưu hành có vốn hóa thị trường 25 nghìn tỷ đồng. Vốn hóa thị trường cho quy mô sơ bộ nhưng không đo lường thanh khoản hoặc liệu dự án có sử dụng thực hay không. Nhiều coin vốn hóa cao có sổ lệnh mỏng; bán số lượng lớn di chuyển giá đáng kể.

sections.h: Staking, lợi suất và halving
p: **Staking** có nghĩa là khóa coin của bạn trong blockchain bằng chứng cổ phần (như Ethereum sau Merge, Cardano hoặc Solana) để giúp xác thực giao dịch. Đổi lại bạn kiếm được phần thưởng, thường được trả bằng cùng loại tiền điện tử. Tỷ lệ dao động từ 3 đến 15 phần trăm hàng năm tùy thuộc vào mạng và tổng số đã stake. Tiền đã stake có thể có thời gian mở khóa từ vài ngày đến vài tuần trong đó bạn không thể bán. **Lợi suất** (yield) rộng hơn: bất kỳ lợi nhuận nào từ việc giữ hoặc cho vay tiền điện tử, bao gồm staking, cung cấp thanh khoản trên DEX (nơi bạn gửi các cặp token vào pool), hoặc cho vay trên các nền tảng như Aave. Lợi suất cao hơn thường có nghĩa là rủi ro cao hơn—lỗi hợp đồng thông minh, biến động giá của token phần thưởng hoặc lừa đảo trắng trợn. Đây không phải là lời khuyên tài chính; đánh giá kiểm toán và hồ sơ theo dõi của từng giao thức.

**Halving** của Bitcoin xảy ra khoảng bốn năm một lần (mỗi 210.000 khối). Phần thưởng khối được trả cho thợ đào cắt một nửa, giảm tốc độ Bitcoin mới vào lưu thông. Halving gần đây nhất vào năm 2024 đã giảm phần thưởng từ 6,25 xuống 3,125 BTC mỗi khối. Halving được tích hợp vào mã Bitcoin và sẽ tiếp tục cho đến khoảng năm 2140, khi nguồn cung giới hạn ở 21 triệu coin. Nhiều nhà giao dịch theo dõi chu kỳ halving để tìm tác động giá tiềm năng, nhưng hiệu suất trong quá khứ không đảm bảo kết quả trong tương lai.

th.title: พจนานุกรมคริปโต: 40 คำศัพท์ที่คุณต้องเข้าใจจริงๆ เพื่อทำความเข้าใจตลาด
th.excerpt: คู่มืออ้างอิงเชิงปฏิบัติสำหรับคำศัพท์สำคัญของการซื้อขายสินทรัพย์ดิจิทัล กระเป๋าเงิน และเทคโนโลยีบลอกเชน ทุกอย่างตั้งแต่คีย์ส่วนตัวไปจนถึงเลเวอเรจ อธิบายเพื่อให้คุณสามารถดำเนินการได้

sections.h: พื้นฐานของกระเป๋าเงิน
p: **กระเป๋าเงิน** (wallet) คือซอฟต์แวร์หรือฮาร์ดแวร์ที่เก็บ **คีย์ส่วนตัว** (private key) ของคุณ ซึ่งเป็นสตริง 64 ตัวอักษรที่พิสูจน์การเป็นเจ้าของสินทรัพย์ดิจิทัลของคุณ หากไม่มีคีย์ส่วนตัว คุณจะไม่สามารถย้ายเงินได้ หากคนอื่นได้มันไป พวกเขาจะเป็นเจ้าของคริปโตของคุณอย่างถาวร—ไม่มีการรีเซ็ตรหัสผ่าน กระเป๋าเงินส่วนใหญ่จะสร้าง **วลีกู้คืน** (seed phrase หรือเรียกว่า recovery phrase หรือ mnemonic) โดยทั่วไปจะเป็น 12 หรือ 24 คำทั่วไปในลำดับเฉพาะ วลีนี้เป็นการสำรองข้อมูลคีย์ส่วนตัวของคุณที่มนุษย์อ่านได้ เขียนลงกระดาษ เก็บไว้อย่างปลอดภัยแบบออฟไลน์ และอย่าถ่ายภาพหรือเก็บไว้ในรูปแบบดิจิทัล ใครก็ตามที่มีวลีกู้คืนของคุณจะควบคุมเงินของคุณ

กระเป๋าเงินมีหลายประเภท **กระเป๋าร้อน** (hot wallet) เชื่อมต่ออินเทอร์เน็ตตลอดเวลา (แอปมือถือ ส่วนขยายเบราว์เซอร์ ซอฟต์แวร์เดสก์ท็อป) และให้ความสำคัญกับความสะดวกสบายสำหรับการซื้อขายบ่อยๆ **กระเป๋าเย็น** (cold wallet) อยู่แบบออฟไลน์—ไม่ว่าจะเป็นอุปกรณ์ฮาร์ดแวร์เช่น Ledger หรือ Trezor หรือแม้แต่กระดาษที่พิมพ์คีย์ของคุณ การจัดเก็บแบบเย็นช่วยลดความเสี่ยงจากการแฮ็กอย่างมากและเป็นมาตรฐานสำหรับการถือครองระยะยาว **กระเป๋าแบบดูแล** (custodial wallet) ให้บริการโดยแพลตฟอร์มซื้อขาย บริษัทถือคีย์ส่วนตัว คุณต้องเชื่อใจพวกเขาในการถอนเงิน **กระเป๋าแบบไม่ดูแล** (non-custodial wallet) ให้คุณควบคุมและรับผิดชอบอย่างเต็มที่ หากสูญเสียวลีกู้คืนกับกระเป๋าแบบไม่ดูแล เงินของคุณจะหายไปตลอดกาล ไม่มีบริษัทใดสามารถกู้คืนได้

sections.h: แพลตฟอร์มซื้อขายและวิธีการซื้อขาย
p: **แพลตฟอร์มซื้อขายแบบรวมศูนย์** (CEX) เช่น Bitkub, Zipmex หรือ Satang Pro เป็นบริษัทที่เก็บคริปโตของคุณในกระเป๋าแบบดูแล จับคู่ผู้ซื้อกับผู้ขาย และมักต้องการการยืนยันตัวตน **Know Your Customer** (KYC)—อัปโหลดบัตรประชาชนหรือหนังสือเดินทาง และบางครั้งหลักฐานที่อยู่ กฎ **ป้องกันการฟอกเงิน** (AML) แตกต่างกันไปตามเขตอำนาจศาล แต่โดยทั่วไปต้องการให้แพลตฟอร์มซื้อขายรายงานธุรกรรมขนาดใหญ่หรือน่าสงสัย กฎเหล่านี้เปลี่ยนแปลงบ่อยครั้ง และนี่ไม่ใช่คำแนะนำทางกฎหมาย ตรวจสอบกฎระเบียบปัจจุบันในที่ที่คุณอาศัยอยู่

**แพลตฟอร์มซื้อขายแบบกระจายศูนย์** (DEX) เช่น Uniswap หรือ PancakeSwap ทำงานบนสมาร์ทคอนแทรกต์โดยไม่มีบริษัทอยู่ตรงกลาง คุณเชื่อมต่อกระเป๋าแบบไม่ดูแลของคุณ ซื้อขายโดยตรงจากมัน และจ่าย **ค่าแก๊ส** (gas fee)—ค่าธรรมเนียมธุรกรรมเครือข่ายที่จ่ายให้ผู้ตรวจสอบบลอกเชน มักเป็น ETH บน Ethereum หรือ BNB บน BNB Smart Chain ค่าแก๊สผันผวนตามความแออัดของเครือข่าย มีตั้งแต่ต่ำกว่า 30 บาทจนถึงมากกว่า 3,000 บาทในช่วงเวลาที่มีการใช้งานสูงสุด DEX ไม่ค่อยต้องการ KYC แต่คุณต้องรับผิดชอบอย่างเต็มที่สำหรับข้อผิดพลาด ส่งเงินไปยังที่อยู่ผิดและไม่สามารถกู้คืนได้

เมื่อคุณทำ **คำสั่งตลาด** (market order) คุณซื้อหรือขายทันทีที่ราคาที่ดีที่สุดที่มี **คำสั่งจำกัด** (limit order) จะดำเนินการเฉพาะที่ราคาที่คุณเลือกหรือดีกว่า ดังนั้นคุณอาจรออย่างไม่มีกำหนดหากตลาดไม่เคยถึง **สเปรด** (spread) คือช่องว่างระหว่างข้อเสนอซื้อสูงสุดและข้อเสนอขายต่ำสุด สเปรดที่แน่นหมายถึงต้นทุนที่ต่ำกว่า **Slippage** เกิดขึ้นเมื่อคำสั่งของคุณใหญ่พอที่จะเคลื่อนย้ายราคาในขณะที่ดำเนินการ หรือเมื่อราคาเปลี่ยนระหว่างการคลิกและการยืนยัน Slippage พบได้บ่อยในคู่สภาพคล่องต่ำและใน DEX ในช่วงความผันผวน

sections.h: เลเวอเรจ ฟิวเจอร์ส และการชำระบัญชี
p: **การซื้อขายแบบสปอต** (spot trading) หมายถึงการซื้อสินทรัพย์ดิจิทัลจริงที่อยู่ในกระเป๋าเงินของคุณ **ฟิวเจอร์ส** (futures) เป็นสัญญาซื้อหรือขายในราคาที่กำหนดในวันที่ในอนาคต และคุณไม่ได้เป็นเจ้าของสินทรัพย์อ้างอิง—เป็นเพียงสัญญา ฟิวเจอร์สช่วยให้คุณใช้ **เลเวอเรจ** (leverage) ยืมเป็นเท่าตัวของเงินทุนของคุณ เลเวอเรจ 10 เท่าเปลี่ยน 3,000 บาทให้เป็นการเปิดรับตลาด 30,000 บาท กำไรเพิ่มขึ้นเป็นทวีคูณ แต่การขาดทุนก็เช่นกัน หากตลาดเคลื่อนที่ต่อต้านคุณ 10 เปอร์เซ็นต์บนเลเวอเรจ 10 เท่า เงินเดิมพันทั้งหมดของคุณหายไป

**การชำระบัญชี** (liquidation) เกิดขึ้นเมื่อการขาดทุนกัดกินมาร์จิ้น (หลักประกันที่คุณฝาก) แพลตฟอร์มซื้อขายหรือโปรโตคอลจะปิดสถานะของคุณโดยอัตโนมัติเพื่อป้องกันไม่ให้คุณเป็นหนี้มากกว่าที่คุณฝาก ราคาชำระบัญชีคำนวณในเวลาที่คุณเปิดสถานะที่มีเลเวอเรจ หาก Bitcoin ลดลงจาก 1,200,000 บาทเป็น 1,080,000 บาทและราคาชำระบัญชีของคุณคือ 1,095,000 บาท คุณจะสูญเสียทุกอย่างก่อนที่ตลาดจะแตะ 1,080,000 บาท ฟิวเจอร์สและเลเวอเรจเป็นเครื่องมือความเสี่ยงสูง ผู้ค้าปลีกจำนวนมากขาดทุน และนี่ไม่ใช่คำแนะนำการลงทุน

sections.h: บลอกเชน เลเยอร์ และสะพานเชื่อม
p: **บลอกเชน** (blockchain) เป็นบันทึกธุรกรรมที่ใช้ร่วมกัน คัดลอกไปยังคอมพิวเตอร์หลายพันเครื่อง (โหนด) บลอกธุรกรรมใหม่แต่ละบลอกเชื่อมโยงทางการเข้ารหัสกับบลอกก่อนหน้า ทำให้บันทึกในอดีตเกือบจะเปลี่ยนแปลงไม่ได้ **Bitcoin** ใช้บลอกเชนหนึ่ง **Ethereum** ใช้อีกอันหนึ่ง แต่ละอันประมวลผลธุรกรรมแตกต่างกันและเรียกเก็บค่าธรรมเนียมของตนเอง

เครือข่าย **Layer 2** (L2) เช่น Arbitrum, Optimism หรือ Polygon อยู่ด้านบนของเชนหลัก (Layer 1) และรวมธุรกรรมจำนวนมากก่อนจะชำระบนเลเยอร์ฐาน L2 ลดค่าแก๊สและเพิ่มความเร็วในการยืนยัน แต่เพิ่มการแลกเปลี่ยนด้านความไว้วางใจหรือความซับซ้อนขึ้นอยู่กับการออกแบบ **สะพาน** (bridge) ย้ายสินทรัพย์ระหว่างบลอกเชน—ตัวอย่างเช่น การห่อ Bitcoin เพื่อใช้บน Ethereum สะพานพึ่งพาสมาร์ทคอนแทรกต์หรือผู้ดูแล หลายแห่งถูกแฮ็กไปหลายร้อยล้านดอลลาร์ ใช้สะพานเฉพาะจำนวนที่คุณสามารถสูญเสียได้ และศึกษาโมเดลความปลอดภัยของสะพานก่อนใช้งาน

sections.h: เหรียญ โทเค็น และมูลค่าตลาด
p: **Bitcoin** (BTC) เป็นสกุลเงินดิจิทัลแรก ทุกสกุลอื่นเป็น **altcoin** Altcoin บางตัวเช่น Ethereum (ETH) ใช้บลอกเชนของตัวเอง อื่นๆ เป็น **โทเค็น** ที่สร้างขึ้นบนเชนที่มีอยู่โดยใช้มาตรฐานเช่น ERC-20 (Ethereum) หรือ BEP-20 (BNB Chain) **Stablecoin** เป็นโทเค็นที่ออกแบบมาเพื่อรักษามูลค่าคงที่ มักจะผูกหนึ่งต่อหนึ่งกับดอลลาร์สหรัฐ USDT (Tether) และ USDC (Circle) ได้รับการสนับสนุนโดยสำรองเงินสดและพันธบัตร แม้ว่าคุณภาพและการตรวจสอบสำรองจะแตกต่างกัน DAI เป็นอัลกอริทึม ได้รับการสนับสนุนโดยหลักประกันคริปโตที่ล็อกในสมาร์ทคอนแทรกต์ Stablecoin ทำให้การซื้อขายและการเก็บมูลค่าง่ายขึ้น แต่การกำกับดูแลด้านกฎระเบียบกำลังเพิ่มขึ้นและบางตัวสูญเสียการผูกราคาระหว่างวิกฤต

**มูลค่าตลาด** (market cap) คูณราคาปัจจุบันด้วยอุปทานที่หมุนเวียน เหรียญที่ราคา 64 บาทพร้อมโทเค็นที่หมุนเวียน 500 ล้านมีมูลค่าตลาด 32,000 ล้านบาท มูลค่าตลาดให้ขนาดคร่าวๆ แต่ไม่ได้วัดสภาพคล่องหรือว่าโครงการมีการใช้งานจริงหรือไม่ เหรียญที่มีมูลค่าตลาดสูงหลายเหรียญมีสมุดคำสั่งบาง การขายจำนวนมากเคลื่อนย้ายราคาอย่างมีนัยสำคัญ

sections.h: การ Stake ผลตอบแทน และ Halving
p: **การ Stake** (staking) หมายถึงการล็อกเหรียญของคุณในบลอกเชนแบบ proof-of-stake (เช่น Ethereum หลัง Merge, Cardano หรือ Solana) เพื่อช่วยตรวจสอบธุรกรรม ในทางกลับคุณจะได้รับรางวัล โดยทั่วไปจ่ายในสกุลเงินดิจิทัลเดียวกัน อัตราแตกต่างกันไปตั้งแต่ 3 ถึง 15 เปอร์เซ็นต์ต่อปีขึ้นอยู่กับเครือข่ายและจำนวนที่ stake ไว้ทั้งหมด เงินที่ stake ไว้อาจมีระยะเวลา unbonding หลายวันหรือหลายสัปดาห์ซึ่งคุณไม่สามารถขายได้ **ผลตอบแทน** (yield) กว้างขึ้น ผลตอบแทนใดๆ จากการถือครองหรือการให้กู้ยืมคริปโต รวมถึงการ stake การให้สภาพคล่องใน DEX (ที่คุณฝากคู่โทเค็นเข้าพูล) หรือการให้กู้ยืมบนแพลตฟอร์มเช่น Aave ผลตอบแทนที่สูงขึ้นมักหมายถึงความเสี่ยงที่สูงขึ้น—ข้อบกพร่องของสมาร์ทคอนแทรกต์ ความผันผวนของราคาของโทเค็นรางวัล หรือการหลอกลวงโดยตรง นี่ไม่ใช่คำแนะนำทางการเงิน ประเมินการตรวจสอบและประวัติติดตามของแต่ละโปรโตคอล

**Halving** ของ Bitcoin เกิดขึ้นประมาณทุกสี่ปี (ทุก 210,000 บลอก) รางวัลบลอกที่จ่ายให้ผู้ขุดลดลงครึ่งหนึ่ง ลดอัตราการเข้าสู่การหมุนเวียนของ Bitcoin ใหม่ Halving ล่าสุดในปี 2024 ลดรางวัลจาก 6.25 เป็น 3.125 BTC ต่อบลอก Halving ถูกสร้างขึ้นในโค้ด Bitcoin และจะดำเนินต่อไปจนถึงประมาณปี 2140 เมื่ออุปทานจำกัดที่ 21 ล้านเหรียญ ผู้ค้าจำนวนมากติดตามวงจร halving สำหรับผลกระทบด้านราคาที่อาจเกิดขึ้น แต่ผลการดำเนินงานในอดีตไม่ได้รับประกันผลลัพธ์ในอนาคต

fr.title: Comment acheter des cryptomonnaies en France : enregistrement PSAN, virements SEPA, KYC et fiscalité
fr.excerpt: La France impose l'enregistrement PSAN auprès de l'AMF et applique une flat tax de 30 % sur les plus-values crypto. Ce guide détaille comment vérifier l'enregistrement, approvisionner votre compte par SEPA, finaliser le KYC et respecter vos obligations fiscales.

sections.h: Vérifier l'enregistrement PSAN avant tout dépôt
p: La France impose un registre national obligatoire pour les prestataires de services sur actifs numériques, appelé PSAN, géré par l'Autorité des marchés financiers (AMF). Toute plateforme offrant des services de conservation, achat, vente ou échange de cryptomonnaies aux résidents français doit détenir un enregistrement PSAN ou une autorisation équivalente dans le cadre du règlement européen MiCA. Opérer sans enregistrement est illégal, et les plateformes non enregistrées ne peuvent pas faire de publicité en France.

Avant de déposer des euros ou de fournir vos documents d'identité, consultez le registre public de l'AMF sur amf-france.org. Le registre distingue les enregistrements obligatoires et les enregistrements optionnels renforcés ; ces derniers ont subi des contrôles supplémentaires sur la lutte anti-blanchiment, l'adéquation des fonds propres et la gouvernance. Recherchez les plateformes avec « enregistrement PSAN » ou « agrément PSAN ». Si une plateforme n'apparaît pas et ne détient pas de licence MiCA délivrée par un autre régulateur européen, ne l'utilisez pas. Parmi les plateformes enregistrées PSAN figurent Bitstamp, Crypto.com, Coinhouse et Paymium ; de nombreuses autres détiennent un passeport MiCA délivré en Irlande, Lituanie ou ailleurs dans l'UE et peuvent servir légalement les clients français sans enregistrement AMF distinct.

sections.h: Approvisionner votre compte : virements SEPA et cartes bancaires
p: La plupart des plateformes enregistrées PSAN ou autorisées MiCA acceptent les dépôts en euros par virement SEPA (espace unique de paiement en euros). Les virements SEPA sont gratuits du côté de votre banque pour les comptes en zone euro, arrivent généralement sous un jour ouvré et n'entraînent aucuns frais de conversion. Pour déposer, vous générez un code de référence SEPA unique ou un IBAN dans votre compte plateforme, puis vous lancez le virement depuis votre banque française. Le nom du compte à l'établissement destinataire doit correspondre à votre nom vérifié sur la plateforme pour respecter les règles anti-blanchiment.

Les paiements par carte bancaire—débit ou crédit—sont disponibles sur de nombreuses plateformes mais entraînent des frais plus élevés, souvent entre 1,5 % et 3,9 % par transaction. Certaines banques françaises bloquent les paiements par carte vers les plateformes crypto par mesure anti-fraude, donc le virement SEPA reste la méthode la plus fiable. Le virement SEPA instantané, lorsqu'il est disponible, peut créditer votre compte en quelques secondes mais peut entraîner de légers frais. Le retrait vers votre compte bancaire français utilise les mêmes rails SEPA et est généralement gratuit ou coûte un forfait nominal de un à trois euros.

sections.h: Exigences KYC et vérification des documents
p: Les directives européennes anti-blanchiment et la réglementation française obligent toutes les plateformes à effectuer des contrôles KYC (connaissance client) avant que vous ne puissiez déposer des montants significatifs ou trader. Vous devrez fournir une pièce d'identité avec photo valide—typiquement une carte nationale d'identité française, un passeport ou un titre de séjour—et un justificatif de domicile de moins de trois mois. Les justificatifs acceptés incluent les factures de services publics (électricité, gaz, eau), les relevés bancaires, les avis d'imposition ou les contrats de location. Les factures de téléphone mobile et les attestations d'assurance sont généralement acceptées si elles affichent vos nom complet et adresse actuelle.

La vérification est généralement automatisée : vous téléchargez des photos ou scans, parfois via une application mobile avec détection de vivacité pour confirmer que vous êtes le détenteur du document. Le traitement prend de quelques minutes à plusieurs jours selon le volume de la plateforme et la qualité des documents. Certaines plateformes imposent des limites de dépôt ou retrait jusqu'à ce que la vérification soit finalisée. Si vous détenez une double nationalité, utilisez le document d'identité français ou européen pour éviter toute confusion. Les plateformes peuvent demander des informations supplémentaires si vous êtes assujetti fiscal américain, personne politiquement exposée, ou si vos schémas de transaction déclenchent une diligence renforcée.

sections.h: Frais de transaction, spreads et coûts de dépôt
p: Les structures tarifaires varient selon les plateformes mais se répartissent généralement en trois catégories : frais maker-taker, frais en pourcentage simple ou tarification par spread. Les modèles maker-taker facturent des frais plus bas (souvent 0,10 % à 0,40 %) lorsque vous placez des ordres limites qui ajoutent de la liquidité au carnet d'ordres, et des frais plus élevés (0,20 % à 0,60 %) lorsque vous prenez de la liquidité avec des ordres au marché. Les modèles à pourcentage fixe appliquent le même taux quel que soit le type d'ordre, couramment 0,50 % à 1,50 %. Les plateformes à spread affichent un prix d'achat ou de vente unique mais intègrent une marge—souvent 0,50 % à 2 %—entre le taux du marché et le prix que vous payez.

Les dépôts SEPA sont gratuits sur la plupart des plateformes ; les retraits SEPA vont de gratuit à environ trois euros. Les dépôts par carte entraînent les frais de 1,5 % à 3,9 % mentionnés précédemment. Certaines plateformes facturent des frais de réseau lorsque vous retirez des cryptomonnaies vers un portefeuille externe ; ces frais reflètent le coût de transaction blockchain (frais de gas sur Ethereum, sat/vbyte sur Bitcoin) et varient selon la congestion du réseau. Comparez toujours le coût global—frais de dépôt, frais de transaction, spread, frais de retrait—plutôt que les seuls taux de transaction affichés.

sections.h: Fiscalité : la flat tax de 30 % sur les plus-values crypto
p: La France impose les plus-values sur cryptomonnaies comme revenus de capitaux mobiliers selon le prélèvement forfaitaire unique (PFU), un taux forfaitaire de 30 % qui inclut 12,8 % d'impôt sur le revenu et 17,2 % de prélèvements sociaux. La plus-value imposable est calculée à chaque fois que vous cédez des cryptomonnaies—que vous vendiez contre des euros, échangiez une crypto contre une autre ou utilisiez de la crypto pour payer des biens ou services. L'impôt s'applique à la différence entre votre coût d'acquisition total (prix d'achat plus frais associés) et le produit de cession, proratisé sur l'ensemble de vos avoirs de cet actif.

Vous déclarez les gains et pertes sur le formulaire 2086, déposé avec votre déclaration annuelle de revenus (formulaire 2042). Le formulaire exige de lister chaque cession, la date, le produit et le prix de revient proratisé. Si le montant annuel total de vos cessions de crypto dépasse certains seuils, la déclaration devient obligatoire même en l'absence de gain net. Les pertes peuvent compenser les gains dans la même année fiscale mais ne peuvent pas être reportées sur les années futures sous le régime du PFU. Alternativement, vous pouvez opter pour le barème progressif de l'impôt sur le revenu si votre taux marginal est inférieur à 12,8 %, mais ce choix s'applique à tous les revenus de capitaux mobiliers de cette année et vous devez exercer l'option lors du dépôt. Les règles fiscales évoluent, et ceci n'est pas un conseil fiscal ; consultez un expert-comptable pour votre situation spécifique.

sections.h: Déclaration des comptes étrangers et plateformes
p: Si vous détenez un compte sur une plateforme de cryptomonnaies située hors de France—c'est-à-dire que le siège, la société exploitante ou l'entité dépositaire de la plateforme n'est pas en France—vous devez déclarer ce compte annuellement sur le formulaire 3916-bis, même si le solde est nul ou si vous n'avez effectué aucune transaction. Cette obligation découle des règles anti-blanchiment et anti-évasion fiscale et s'applique aux comptes ouverts, détenus, utilisés ou clôturés durant l'année fiscale. Chaque compte plateforme étranger nécessite une ligne distincte sur le formulaire.

Le formulaire 3916-bis demande le nom de la plateforme, l'adresse, le pays, la référence ou le numéro de compte, les dates d'ouverture et de clôture, et la nature du compte. De nombreuses plateformes connues—Binance, Kraken, Coinbase—ont leur siège hors de France et déclenchent cette obligation. Le défaut de déclaration des comptes étrangers peut entraîner des pénalités à partir de 750 euros par compte non déclaré, montant à 1 500 euros si le compte se trouve dans une juridiction non coopérative. La déclaration est purement informative ; elle ne remplace pas le formulaire 2086 pour la déclaration des gains. Les plateformes domestiques enregistrées PSAN en France ne nécessitent pas de déclaration 3916-bis.

sections.h: Choisir une plateforme : enregistrement, liquidité et support
p: Lors du choix d'une plateforme, privilégiez l'enregistrement PSAN ou MiCA, puis évaluez la liquidité, les frais et le support client. Une liquidité élevée—visible par des écarts achat-vente serrés et des carnets d'ordres profonds—signifie que vous pouvez acheter ou vendre sans déplacer significativement le prix, ce qui compte davantage à mesure que la taille de transaction augmente. Les plateformes avec support en français et des équipes de service client familières avec les exigences de l'AMF résoudront les problèmes plus rapidement, notamment lors de difficultés KYC ou de retrait.

Réfléchissez si vous souhaitez conserver vos cryptomonnaies sur la plateforme (garde déléguée) ou les transférer vers un portefeuille privé (auto-garde). Les comptes en garde déléguée sont plus simples mais comportent le risque que la plateforme contrôle vos clés ; si la plateforme devient insolvable ou gèle les comptes, l'accès à vos fonds peut être retardé ou perdu. L'auto-garde exige de gérer vos phrases de récupération et clés privées de manière sécurisée ; les perdre signifie perdre l'accès définitivement. Certains investisseurs répartissent leurs avoirs entre portefeuilles chauds pour le trading et stockage froid pour la détention long terme. Aucune approche n'est sans risque, et le bon équilibre dépend de votre confiance technique et des montants en jeu.

en.title: How to Buy Cryptocurrency in France: PSAN Registration, Payment Methods, KYC and Tax Obligations
en.excerpt: France requires crypto platforms to register with the AMF as PSANs and applies a 30% flat tax on gains. This guide covers how to verify registration, fund your account via SEPA, complete KYC, and meet your tax reporting obligations.

sections.h: Verify PSAN Registration Before Depositing Funds
p: France operates a mandatory national register for crypto service providers called PSAN (Prestataires de Services sur Actifs Numériques), managed by the Autorité des marchés financiers (AMF). Any platform offering custody, buying, selling, or exchange services to French residents must either hold PSAN registration or an equivalent EU authorization under MiCA. Operating without registration is illegal, and unregistered platforms cannot legally advertise in France.

Before you deposit euros or provide identity documents, check the AMF public register at amf-france.org. The register lists both mandatory registrants and optional registrants; the latter have undergone additional compliance reviews covering anti-money-laundering controls, capital adequacy, and governance. Look for platforms with "enregistrement PSAN" or "agrément PSAN." If a platform is not listed and does not hold a MiCA license from another EU regulator, do not use it. Major platforms registered as PSAN include Bitstamp, Crypto.com, Coinhouse, and Paymium; many others hold MiCA passports from regulators in Ireland, Lithuania, or other EU jurisdictions and can legally serve French clients without separate AMF registration.

sections.h: Funding Your Account: SEPA Transfers and Card Payments
p: Most PSAN-registered and MiCA-authorized platforms accept euro deposits via SEPA (Single Euro Payments Area) bank transfer. SEPA transfers are free from your bank's perspective for euro-zone accounts, usually arrive within one business day, and carry no currency conversion fees. To deposit, you generate a unique SEPA reference code or IBAN in your platform account, then initiate the transfer from your French bank. The account name at the receiving institution must match your verified name on the platform to comply with anti-money-laundering rules.

Card payments—both debit and credit—are available on many platforms but typically incur higher fees, often between 1.5% and 3.9% per transaction. Some French banks block card payments to crypto platforms as a fraud-prevention measure, so SEPA transfers remain the most reliable method. Instant SEPA, where available, can credit your account within seconds but may carry a small platform fee. Withdrawal back to your French bank account uses the same SEPA rails and is usually free or costs a nominal flat fee of one to three euros.

sections.h: KYC Requirements and Document Verification
p: EU anti-money-laundering directives and French regulations require all platforms to perform Know Your Customer (KYC) checks before you can deposit significant sums or trade. You will need to provide a valid government-issued photo ID—typically a French carte nationale d'identité, passport, or residence permit—and proof of address dated within the last three months. Accepted proof-of-address documents include utility bills (electricity, gas, water), bank statements, tax notices (avis d'imposition), or rental agreements. Mobile phone bills and insurance statements are usually accepted if they show your full name and current address.

Verification is usually automated: you upload photos or scans, sometimes using a mobile app with liveness detection to confirm you are the document holder. Processing takes anywhere from a few minutes to several days depending on platform volume and document quality. Some platforms impose deposit or withdrawal limits until verification is complete. If you hold dual nationality, use the French or EU identity document to avoid confusion. Platforms may request additional information if you are a US person for tax purposes, a politically exposed person, or if transaction patterns trigger enhanced due diligence.

sections.h: Trading Fees, Spreads and Deposit Costs
p: Fee structures vary by platform but generally fall into three categories: maker-taker trading fees, simple percentage fees, or spread-based pricing. Maker-taker models charge lower fees (often 0.10% to 0.40%) when you place limit orders that add liquidity to the order book, and higher fees (0.20% to 0.60%) when you take liquidity with market orders. Flat percentage models apply the same rate regardless of order type, commonly 0.50% to 1.50%. Spread-based platforms show a single buy or sell price but embed a margin—often 0.50% to 2%—between the market rate and the price you pay.

SEPA deposits are free on most platforms; SEPA withdrawals range from free to around three euros. Card deposits carry the 1.5% to 3.9% fees mentioned earlier. Some platforms charge network fees when you withdraw cryptocurrency to an external wallet; these fees reflect the blockchain transaction cost (gas fees on Ethereum, sat/vbyte on Bitcoin) and vary with network congestion. Always compare the all-in cost—deposit fee, trading fee, spread, withdrawal fee—rather than headline trading rates alone.

sections.h: Tax Treatment: The 30% Flat Tax on Crypto Gains
p: France taxes cryptocurrency gains as capital income under the prélèvement forfaitaire unique (PFU), a flat rate of 30% that includes 12.8% income tax and 17.2% social contributions. The taxable gain is calculated each time you dispose of cryptocurrency—whether you sell for euros, trade one crypto for another, or use crypto to pay for goods and services. The tax applies to the difference between your total acquisition cost (purchase price plus associated fees) and the disposal proceeds, prorated across your entire holdings of that asset.

You report gains and losses on form 2086, filed alongside your annual income tax declaration (form 2042). The form requires you to list each disposal, the date, the proceeds, and the prorated cost basis. If your total annual proceeds from crypto disposals exceed certain thresholds, reporting becomes mandatory even if you have no net gain. Losses can offset gains within the same tax year but cannot be carried forward to future years under the PFU regime. Alternatively, you may opt for the progressive income tax scale (barème progressif) if your marginal rate is lower than 12.8%, but this choice applies to all capital income for that year and you must make the election when filing. Tax rules change, and this is not tax advice; consult a French tax professional (expert-comptable) for your specific situation.

sections.h: Declaring Foreign Accounts and Platforms
p: If you hold an account on a cryptocurrency platform located outside France—meaning the platform's headquarters, operating company, or custodial entity is not in France—you must declare that account annually on form 3916-bis, even if the account balance is zero or you made no transactions. This requirement stems from anti-money-laundering and tax-evasion rules and applies to accounts opened, held, used, or closed during the tax year. Each foreign platform account requires a separate line on the form.

Form 3916-bis asks for the platform name, address, country, account reference or number, opening and closing dates, and the nature of the account. Many well-known platforms—Binance, Kraken, Coinbase—are headquartered outside France and trigger this obligation. Failure to declare foreign accounts can result in penalties starting at 750 euros per undeclared account, rising to 1,500 euros if the account is in a non-cooperative jurisdiction. The declaration is purely informational; it does not replace the 2086 form for reporting gains. Domestic platforms registered as PSAN in France do not require 3916-bis reporting.

sections.h: Choosing a Platform: Registration, Liquidity and Support
p: When selecting a platform, prioritize PSAN or MiCA registration, then evaluate liquidity, fees, and customer support. High liquidity—visible as tight bid-ask spreads and deep order books—means you can buy or sell without significantly moving the price, which matters more as trade size increases. Platforms with French-language support and customer service teams familiar with AMF requirements will resolve issues faster, especially during KYC or withdrawal problems.

Consider whether you want to keep cryptocurrency on the platform (custodial) or move it to a private wallet (self-custody). Custodial accounts are simpler but carry the risk that the platform controls your keys; if the platform becomes insolvent or freezes accounts, access to your funds may be delayed or lost. Self-custody requires you to manage seed phrases and private keys securely; losing them means losing access permanently. Some investors split holdings between hot wallets for trading and cold storage for long-term holdings. No approach is risk-free, and the right balance depends on your technical confidence and the amounts involved.

pt.title: Como Comprar Criptomoedas no Brasil: Depósitos via PIX, Regulamentação, KYC e Impostos
pt.excerpt: O Brasil regulamenta prestadores de serviços de ativos virtuais através do Banco Central, nos termos da Lei 14.478. Este guia cobre tudo o que você precisa saber sobre como comprar cripto com reais, desde depósitos via PIX e requisitos de KYC até imposto sobre ganhos de capital e obrigações mensais de declaração.

sections.h: Marco Legal e Regulamentação
p: O Brasil formalizou a regulamentação de criptomoedas através da Lei 14.478/2022, que coloca os prestadores de serviços de ativos virtuais sob supervisão do Banco Central. Exchanges, corretoras e serviços de custódia operando no Brasil devem se registrar junto ao Banco Central e cumprir padrões de combate à lavagem de dinheiro. A lei não classifica criptomoedas como moeda de curso legal, mas as trata como ativos sujeitos a obrigações específicas de declaração e tributação.

Enquanto o Banco Central supervisiona a conformidade operacional, questões tributárias ficam a cargo da Receita Federal. Essa estrutura dupla significa que as plataformas devem satisfazer tanto regulamentos prudenciais quanto requisitos de transparência fiscal. As regras e sua interpretação continuam a evoluir conforme o Banco Central emite instruções normativas, portanto verifique os requisitos atuais com a plataforma escolhida ou consulte um profissional tributário brasileiro familiarizado com ativos digitais.

sections.h: Comprando Cripto com PIX e TED
p: A maioria das exchanges brasileiras aceita depósitos em reais via PIX e TED (transferência bancária). O PIX normalmente liquida em segundos, permitindo que você negocie imediatamente após o depósito ser confirmado pela plataforma. Transferências TED geralmente chegam no mesmo dia útil se iniciadas durante o horário bancário, embora algumas plataformas possam aplicar uma breve retenção de verificação em depósitos de primeira vez.

O cadastro na plataforma normalmente exige vincular uma conta bancária registrada no seu CPF. Após a verificação, você gera uma chave PIX ou QR code dentro da interface da exchange, ou copia os dados bancários da plataforma para uma TED. Os depósitos mínimos variam por plataforma—algumas aceitam a partir de R$10, enquanto outras estabelecem pisos de R$50 ou R$100. O saque de reais de volta para sua conta bancária segue os mesmos trilhos: saques via PIX costumam chegar em minutos, saques via TED em até um dia útil.

sections.h: Requisitos de KYC e Verificação de CPF
p: Todas as exchanges brasileiras regulamentadas aplicam procedimentos de Conheça Seu Cliente (KYC). No mínimo, você fornecerá seu CPF (Cadastro de Pessoas Físicas), nome completo, data de nascimento e um documento de identidade com foto emitido pelo governo, como RG (Registro Geral) ou CNH (carteira de motorista). Muitas plataformas também exigem comprovante de residência—uma conta de luz, extrato bancário ou correspondência oficial datada dos últimos três meses.

Os prazos de verificação variam de alguns minutos a vários dias úteis, dependendo do processo da plataforma e se uma revisão manual é acionada. Algumas exchanges usam leitura automatizada de documentos e reconhecimento facial para agilizar a aprovação; outras colocam as submissões em fila para revisão humana. Limites de transação mais altos ou acesso a recursos avançados como negociação com margem normalmente requerem KYC aprimorado, que pode incluir declarações de renda ou documentos de identidade adicionais. Mantenha cópias dos documentos enviados, pois a Receita Federal pode solicitar comprovação de identidade ao revisar suas declarações de transações cripto.

sections.h: Taxas e Spreads em Pares BRL
p: As exchanges brasileiras cobram taxas através de vários modelos: comissões de negociação, taxas de depósito/saque e spreads de compra-venda em pares BRL. As taxas de negociação normalmente variam de 0,1% a 1,5% por transação, frequentemente estruturadas em camadas maker-taker, onde ordens passivas (maker) pagam menos que ordens a mercado (taker). Descontos baseados em volume são comuns—traders que movimentam volumes mensais mais altos em reais ou mantêm o token nativo da plataforma podem receber taxas reduzidas.

Depósitos via PIX geralmente são gratuitos, embora algumas plataformas limitem o número de depósitos gratuitos por mês ou cobrem uma pequena porcentagem sobre valores acima de um limite. Saques via PIX ou TED podem incorrer em taxas fixas de R$3 a R$10, ou taxas percentuais em torno de 0,5% a 1%. Preste atenção especial ao spread em pares de negociação BRL como BTC/BRL ou USDT/BRL. Spreads mais amplos efetivamente aumentam seu custo, especialmente em pares de menor liquidez ou durante períodos voláteis. Comparar o custo total—taxa mais spread—entre plataformas para o tamanho típico de sua operação oferece uma visão mais clara do que apenas as taxas de comissão anunciadas.

sections.h: Declaração Mensal à Receita Federal (IN 1.888)
p: A Instrução Normativa 1.888 obriga exchanges operando no Brasil a reportar mensalmente à Receita Federal todas as transações dos usuários. Esse reporte cobre compras, vendas, transferências e quaisquer outras operações envolvendo criptoativos. As plataformas enviam esses relatórios automaticamente; usuários individuais não apresentam esta obrigação específica, mas devem estar cientes de que a autoridade fiscal recebe um registro detalhado da atividade vinculada ao seu CPF.

Como usuário, você tem sua própria obrigação de declaração se o total de suas participações exceder R$5.000 em qualquer momento do ano, ou se você realizar transações acima de certos limites. Você declara essas participações e transações na Declaração de Imposto de Renda anual. Mesmo que não deva imposto—por exemplo, se os ganhos ficarem abaixo da isenção mensal—você ainda deve declarar as participações e alienações com precisão. Deixar de declarar ou subdeclarar pode desencadear multas e juros. Como as regras tributárias e limites estão sujeitos a mudanças, consulte um contador brasileiro com experiência em tributação de criptomoedas para garantir conformidade com os requisitos atuais.

sections.h: Imposto sobre Ganhos de Capital e a Isenção de R$35.000
p: Ganhos de capital na venda de criptomoedas são tributados como investimentos, não como câmbio de moeda. A Receita Federal aplica alíquotas progressivas: 15% sobre ganhos até R$5 milhões, 17,5% de R$5 milhões a R$10 milhões, 20% de R$10 milhões a R$30 milhões e 22,5% acima de R$30 milhões. Essas faixas se aplicam por transação ou por mês, dependendo de como você calcula o ganho.

Existe uma isenção crítica para pessoas físicas: se o total de suas vendas de criptoativos em um determinado mês calendário não exceder R$35.000, quaisquer ganhos dessas vendas estão isentos de imposto. Essa isenção aplica-se apenas a vendas; trocas entre criptomoedas (por exemplo, BTC para ETH) são consideradas alienações e podem gerar um fato gerador mesmo sem converter para reais. Se você vender R$40.000 em um mês, os ganhos sobre o valor total são tributáveis. Cronometrar as vendas para permanecer abaixo do limite mensal pode, portanto, proporcionar economias fiscais significativas, embora você deva documentar cada transação com data, valor, custo de aquisição e preço de venda.

O imposto é autoavaliado e pago via DARF (Documento de Arrecadação de Receitas Federais) até o último dia útil do mês seguinte à venda. Por exemplo, ganhos realizados em março vencem no final de abril. Calcular o custo de aquisição—frequentemente PEPS (primeiro a entrar, primeiro a sair) ou custo médio—requer manutenção cuidadosa de registros, especialmente se você negocia com frequência ou em várias plataformas. A interação da isenção mensal, métodos de custo de aquisição e obrigações de declaração torna a tributação cripto brasileira complexa. Esta é uma informação geral e não constitui assessoria fiscal; as regras mudam e situações individuais variam, portanto orientação profissional é prudente.

sections.h: Escolhendo uma Plataforma e Gerenciando Riscos
p: Ao selecionar uma exchange brasileira, verifique se está registrada junto ao Banco Central e cumpre o reporte da IN 1.888. Plataformas estabelecidas publicam detalhes de registro e mantêm tabelas de taxas transparentes. Compare métodos de depósito e saque, criptomoedas suportadas, liquidez nos pares BRL que você pretende negociar e a qualidade do suporte ao cliente em português.

Recursos de segurança importam: procure autenticação de dois fatores, armazenamento a frio da maioria dos fundos dos usuários e uma política clara sobre seguro ou responsabilidade em caso de violação. Nenhuma plataforma é livre de riscos; hacks de exchanges, insolvência e falhas operacionais ocorreram globalmente. Manter saldos elevados em uma exchange expõe você ao risco de contraparte. Para participações de longo prazo, considere transferir ativos para uma carteira privada onde você controla as chaves, mantendo apenas saldos de negociação na plataforma.

Conformidade regulatória e comunicação transparente são sinais positivos, mas a due diligence permanece sua responsabilidade. Leia avaliações de usuários, teste a plataforma com um depósito pequeno e certifique-se de entender a estrutura de taxas e o processo de saque antes de comprometer capital significativo. O mercado cripto brasileiro é dinâmico, e as plataformas podem mudar políticas, estruturas de taxas ou até sair do mercado, portanto mantenha-se informado e reavalie sua escolha periodicamente.

en.title: How to Buy Cryptocurrency in Brazil: PIX Deposits, Regulation, KYC, Taxes
en.excerpt: Brazil regulates crypto service providers through the Banco Central under Law 14.478. This guide covers everything you need to know about buying crypto with BRL, from PIX deposits and KYC requirements to capital gains tax and monthly reporting obligations.

sections.h: Legal Framework and Regulation
p: Brazil formalized crypto regulation through Law 14.478/2022, which places virtual asset service providers under Banco Central supervision. Exchanges, brokers, and custody services operating in Brazil must register with the central bank and comply with anti-money laundering standards. The law does not classify cryptocurrencies as legal tender but treats them as assets subject to specific reporting and tax obligations.

While the Banco Central oversees operational compliance, tax matters fall under the Receita Federal (Federal Revenue Service). This dual structure means platforms must satisfy both prudential regulations and tax transparency requirements. Rules and their interpretation continue to evolve as the Banco Central issues normative instructions, so verify current requirements with the platform you choose or consult a Brazilian tax professional familiar with digital assets.

sections.h: Buying Crypto with PIX and TED
p: Most Brazilian exchanges accept deposits in reais via PIX and TED (bank transfer). PIX typically settles within seconds, allowing you to trade immediately after the deposit clears on the platform's side. TED transfers usually arrive within the same business day if initiated during banking hours, though some platforms may apply a brief verification hold on first-time deposits.

Platform onboarding typically requires linking a bank account registered in your CPF. After verification, you generate a PIX key or QR code within the exchange interface, or copy the platform's bank details for a TED. Minimum deposits vary by platform—some accept as little as R$10, while others set floors of R$50 or R$100. Withdrawal of reais back to your bank account follows the same rails: PIX withdrawals often arrive in minutes, TED withdrawals within one business day.

sections.h: KYC Requirements and CPF Verification
p: All regulated Brazilian exchanges enforce Know Your Customer (KYC) procedures. At minimum, you will provide your CPF (Cadastro de Pessoas Físicas), full name, date of birth, and a government-issued photo ID such as RG (Registro Geral) or CNH (driver's license). Many platforms also require proof of address—a utility bill, bank statement, or official correspondence dated within the past three months.

Verification times range from a few minutes to several business days, depending on the platform's process and whether manual review is triggered. Some exchanges use automated document scanning and facial recognition to speed approval; others queue submissions for human review. Higher transaction limits or access to advanced features like margin trading typically require enhanced KYC, which may include income declarations or additional identity documents. Keep copies of submitted documents, as the Receita Federal may request proof of identity when reviewing your crypto transaction reports.

sections.h: Fees and Spreads on BRL Pairs
p: Brazilian exchanges charge fees through several models: trading commissions, deposit/withdrawal fees, and bid-ask spreads on BRL pairs. Trading fees typically range from 0.1% to 1.5% per transaction, often structured in maker-taker tiers where passive orders (maker) pay less than market orders (taker). Volume-based discounts are common—traders moving higher monthly volumes in reais or holding the platform's native token may receive reduced rates.

PIX deposits are usually free, though some platforms cap the number of free deposits per month or charge a small percentage on amounts above a threshold. Withdrawals via PIX or TED may incur flat fees of R$3 to R$10, or percentage-based fees around 0.5% to 1%. Pay close attention to the spread on BRL trading pairs like BTC/BRL or USDT/BRL. Wider spreads effectively increase your cost, especially on lower-liquidity pairs or during volatile periods. Comparing the all-in cost—fee plus spread—across platforms for your typical trade size gives a clearer picture than headline commission rates alone.

sections.h: Monthly Reporting to Receita Federal (IN 1.888)
p: Normative Instruction 1.888 obliges exchanges operating in Brazil to report all user transactions monthly to the Receita Federal. This reporting covers purchases, sales, transfers, and any other operations involving crypto assets. Platforms submit these reports automatically; individual users do not file this particular obligation themselves, but should be aware that the tax authority receives a detailed record of activity tied to your CPF.

As a user, you have your own reporting duty if your total holdings exceed R$5,000 at any point in the year, or if you conduct transactions above certain thresholds. You declare these holdings and transactions in the annual Declaração de Imposto de Renda (income tax return). Even if you owe no tax—for instance, if gains fall under the monthly exemption—you must still report holdings and disposals accurately. Failure to report or underreporting can trigger fines and interest. Because tax rules and thresholds are subject to change, consult a Brazilian accountant experienced in crypto taxation to ensure compliance with current requirements.

sections.h: Capital Gains Tax and the R$35,000 Exemption
p: Capital gains on cryptocurrency sales are taxed as investimentos, not currency exchange. The Receita Federal applies progressive rates: 15% on gains up to R$5 million, 17.5% from R$5 million to R$10 million, 20% from R$10 million to R$30 million, and 22.5% above R$30 million. These brackets apply per transaction or per month, depending on how you calculate the gain.

A critical exemption exists for individuals: if your total sales of crypto assets in a given calendar month do not exceed R$35,000, any gains from those sales are exempt from tax. This exemption applies only to sales; exchanges between cryptocurrencies (for example, BTC to ETH) are considered disposals and may trigger a taxable event even without converting to reais. If you sell R$40,000 worth in one month, gains on the entire amount are taxable. Timing sales to stay under the monthly threshold can therefore provide significant tax savings, though you should document each transaction with date, amount, cost basis, and sale price.

Tax is self-assessed and paid via DARF (Documento de Arrecadação de Receitas Federais) by the last business day of the month following the sale. For example, gains realized in March are due by the end of April. Calculating cost basis—often FIFO (first in, first out) or average cost—requires careful record-keeping, especially if you trade frequently or across multiple platforms. The interplay of the monthly exemption, cost basis methods, and reporting obligations makes Brazilian crypto taxation complex. This is general information and not tax advice; rules change and individual situations vary, so professional guidance is prudent.

sections.h: Choosing a Platform and Managing Risk
p: When selecting a Brazilian exchange, verify it is registered with the Banco Central and complies with IN 1.888 reporting. Established platforms publish registration details and maintain transparent fee schedules. Compare deposit and withdrawal methods, supported cryptocurrencies, liquidity on the BRL pairs you intend to trade, and the quality of customer support in Portuguese.

Security features matter: look for two-factor authentication, cold storage of the majority of user funds, and a clear policy on insurance or liability in case of breach. No platform is risk-free; exchange hacks, insolvency, and operational failures have occurred globally. Holding large balances on an exchange exposes you to counterparty risk. For long-term holdings, consider transferring assets to a private wallet where you control the keys, keeping only trading balances on the platform.

Regulatory compliance and transparent communication are positive signals, but due diligence remains your responsibility. Read user reviews, test the platform with a small deposit, and ensure you understand the fee structure and withdrawal process before committing significant capital. The Brazilian crypto market is dynamic, and platforms can change policies, fee structures, or even exit the market, so stay informed and reassess your choice periodically.

ja.title: 日本で暗号資産を購入する方法:金融庁登録業者、日本円入金、本人確認、税制の完全ガイド
ja.excerpt: 日本ではすべての暗号資産交換業者が資金決済法に基づき金融庁への登録を義務付けられています。このガイドでは金融庁登録の確認方法、日本円の入金手段、マイナンバーを含む本人確認、手数料体系、そして暗号資産の利益が雑所得として累進課税される仕組みを解説します。

sections.h: 金融庁登録とその重要性
p: 日本の資金決済法では、国内で営業するすべての暗号資産交換業者は金融庁への登録が義務付けられています。この登録により、業者は厳格な資本要件を満たし、顧客資産の分別管理を実施し、堅牢なセキュリティ対策を講じ、定期的な監査を受けることが保証されます。未登録業者の運営は違法であり、金融庁の認可を受けていない海外プラットフォームを利用することは大きなリスクを伴います。

交換業者の登録状況を確認するには、金融庁の公式ウェブサイトで暗号資産交換業者の登録一覧を確認してください。一覧には会社名、登録番号、登録年月日が記載されています。金融庁登録済みの主要な交換業者には、bitFlyer、Coincheck、GMOコイン、DMM Bitcoin、Bitbank、Zaifなどがあります。資金を送金する前に必ず登録を確認してください。金融庁は新規登録や登録抹消に伴いこの一覧を更新します。

sections.h: 口座開設:マイナンバーと本人確認の要件
p: すべての金融庁登録業者は、マネーロンダリング対策規制に基づいて本人確認を実施する必要があります。手続きには運転免許証、在留カード、マイナンバーカードなどの顔写真付き身分証明書が必要です。多くの交換業者はマイナンバー(個人番号)の提出も求めます。マイナンバーカード自体、または通知カードと別の顔写真付き身分証明書の組み合わせで提出できます。

口座開設には通常1〜3営業日かかります。交換業者のウェブサイトまたはモバイルアプリを通じて、画像をアップロードするか、リアルタイム写真認証を利用して書類を提出します。一部の交換業者は追加の確認手段として、登録住所に確認コード付きのハガキを郵送します。外国籍の居住者も、有効な在留カードと日本の住所・電話番号があれば口座を開設できます。税法やコンプライアンス要件は変更されることがあるため、これは法的助言ではありません。最新の規則については交換業者または資格を持つアドバイザーに確認してください。

sections.h: 日本円の入金:銀行振込とコンビニ払い
p: 金融庁登録業者は複数の方法で日本円の入金を受け付けています。銀行振込(振込)が最も一般的で、交換業者は各顧客に専用の振込先口座番号を提供します。三菱UFJ銀行、みずほ銀行、三井住友銀行、りそな銀行、ゆうちょ銀行などの主要銀行から午後の締切時間前に振り込めば、通常は当日中に着金します。インターネットバンキングでの振込は無料または100〜300円程度の手数料がかかります。

多くの交換業者はファミリーマート、ローソン、セブン‐イレブンなどのコンビニエンスストアでの支払いにも対応しています。交換業者のアプリで支払番号またはバーコードを生成し、店舗に持参して現金で支払います。入金は10〜60分以内に交換業者の口座に反映されます。コンビニ入金は1回あたり300〜700円程度の手数料がかかり、1日あたり30万円程度の上限が設定されていることがあります。一部のプラットフォームはネット銀行からのクイック入金やATMからのペイジー決済にも対応しています。銀行口座への出金手数料は、交換業者や金額により200〜750円程度です。

sections.h: 取引手数料とスプレッド
p: 金融庁登録業者は、メイカー・テイカーモデルまたはスプレッドによって手数料を徴収します。BitbankやGMOコインなどのメイカー・テイカー型の交換業者は、流動性を提供する注文(メイカー注文、通常0%〜マイナス0.02%、つまりリベートを受け取れる)と流動性を消費する注文(テイカー注文、通常0.05%〜0.15%)で異なる手数料を設定しています。これらの交換業者では、特定の価格での買い注文と売り注文を確認できる板情報が表示されます。

Coincheckなどのプラットフォームは、スプレッドを含んだ提示価格で売買するシンプルなモデルを採用しています。スプレッドとは買値と売値の差額です。スプレッドは暗号資産や市場状況により変動しますが、通常0.1%〜5%の範囲です。スプレッドが広いほど実質的なコストが高くなります。交換業者を比較する際は、取引手数料と入出金手数料の両方を含めた総コストを計算してください。一部の交換業者はメイカー手数料を無料にしたり、大口取引者向けに手数料を割引したりしています。

sections.h: 税務上の取扱い:暗号資産の利益は雑所得
p: 日本では暗号資産の利益は譲渡所得ではなく、国税庁により雑所得(雑所得)に分類され、5%〜45%の累進所得税率に加えて約10%の住民税が課されます。つまり、給与と暗号資産の利益を含めた年間の総所得が税率を決定します。例えば、合計所得が20%の税率区分に該当する場合、住民税を含めた実効税率は約30%に達します。

各暗号資産取引の利益を計算するには、移動平均法または総平均法などの方法を使用して取得原価を算出する必要があります。暗号資産を別の暗号資産と交換した場合(日本円への売却だけでなく)も、その取引は課税対象の所得を発生させます。多くの交換業者は年間取引報告書を提供していますが、正確な計算と申告の責任は利用者にあります。損失は他の雑所得と相殺できますが、給与所得や株式の譲渡所得とは相殺できません。税法は変更されることがあり、計算は複雑になる可能性があるため、これは税務助言ではありません。利益が基礎控除額を超える場合や頻繁に取引する場合は、暗号資産に詳しい日本の税理士(税理士)に相談してください。

sections.h: ニーズに応じた交換業者の選び方
p: 交換業者によって適した用途が異なります。BitbankやGMOコインは板情報を備えた本格的な取引画面、アクティブトレーダー向けの低手数料、幅広い暗号資産を提供しています。Coincheckは初心者に好まれるシンプルなインターフェース、迅速なオンボーディング、簡単なコンビニ入金を備えていますが、スプレッドが広い場合があります。DMM Bitcoinはレバレッジ取引を希望するユーザー向けに特化しています。bitFlyerは保険補償を伴う強固なセキュリティを提供し、簡単な購入と高度な取引の両方に対応しています。

購入したい暗号資産を考慮してください。すべての交換業者が同じ資産を取り扱っているわけではありません。希望する入金方法に対応しているか、手数料が取引規模に適しているかを確認してください。大口購入では、スプレッドが狭い、または手数料率が低い交換業者が有利です。一方、少額で頻度の低い購入では、取引ごとのコストよりも利便性やインターフェースのシンプルさを優先する場合があります。取引スタイルに関わらず、二段階認証、コールドウォレット保管、保険などのセキュリティ機能を選択基準に含めるべきです。

sections.h: セキュリティと資産保護
p: 金融庁の規制により、交換業者は顧客の暗号資産を会社資産と分別管理し、一定水準の純資産を財務的裏付けとして保持する必要があります。ほとんどの交換業者は顧客資産の大部分をコールドウォレット(オフライン保管)に保管し、日々の出金に必要な量だけをホットウォレットに移動しています。これによりハッキングのリスクが軽減されます。bitFlyerなどの一部の交換業者は、不正アクセスやセキュリティ侵害による損失を補償する保険契約を結んでいますが、補償内容や限度額は異なります。

Google AuthenticatorやAuthyなどの認証アプリを使用して二段階認証を有効にしてください。SIMスワップ攻撃に脆弱なSMSよりも安全です。強力で固有のパスワードを使用し、交換業者が対応していればハードウェアセキュリティキーの使用を検討してください。金融庁登録により未規制プラットフォームと比べてリスクは軽減されますが、どの交換業者もセキュリティインシデントから完全に免れるわけではありません。大量の資産を交換業者に長期保管しないでください。多額の保有資産は秘密鍵を自分で管理できる個人用ハードウェアウォレットに移してください。フィッシング攻撃はしばしば交換業者になりすますため、交換業者のURLは常に手動で入力するか、メールのリンクをクリックするのではなくブックマークを使用してください。

en.title: How to Buy Cryptocurrency in Japan: A Complete Guide to FSA-Registered Exchanges, KYC, and Tax Treatment
en.excerpt: Japan requires all cryptocurrency exchanges to register with the Financial Services Agency under the Payment Services Act. This guide covers FSA verification, JPY deposit methods, My Number requirements, fees, and how crypto profits are taxed as miscellaneous income.

sections.h: FSA Registration and Why It Matters
p: Japan's Payment Services Act mandates that all cryptocurrency exchanges operating in the country must register with the Financial Services Agency (FSA). This registration ensures exchanges meet strict capital requirements, maintain segregated customer funds, implement robust security measures, and undergo regular audits. Operating an unregistered exchange is illegal, and residents face significant risk using offshore platforms that lack FSA approval.

To verify an exchange's registration status, visit the FSA's official website and check the list of registered crypto asset exchange service providers (暗号資産交換業者). The list includes company names, registration numbers, and registration dates. Major FSA-registered exchanges include bitFlyer, Coincheck, GMO Coin, DMM Bitcoin, Bitbank, and Zaif. Always confirm registration before transferring funds, as the FSA updates this list when new exchanges register or existing ones lose their license.

sections.h: Opening an Account: My Number and KYC Requirements
p: All FSA-registered exchanges must verify your identity under anti-money laundering regulations. The process requires a government-issued photo ID such as a driver's license, residence card (zairyu card), or My Number card. Most exchanges also require your My Number (Individual Number), which can be provided via the My Number card itself or a notification card (tsuchi card) paired with another photo ID.

Account opening typically takes one to three business days. You'll submit documents through the exchange's website or mobile app, either by uploading images or using real-time photo verification. Some exchanges mail a postcard with an activation code to your registered address as an additional verification step. Foreign residents can open accounts if they hold a valid residence card and have a Japanese address and phone number. Tax laws and compliance requirements change, so this is not legal advice; verify current rules with the exchange or a qualified advisor.

sections.h: Depositing Japanese Yen: Bank Transfers and Convenience Store Options
p: FSA-registered exchanges accept Japanese yen through several methods. Bank transfers (furikomi) are the most common, with exchanges providing dedicated virtual account numbers for each customer. Transfers from major banks like MUFG, Mizuho, Sumitomo Mitsui, Resona, and Japan Post Bank typically arrive within the same business day if sent before the afternoon cutoff. Internet banking transfers are usually free or cost 100 to 300 yen depending on your bank.

Many exchanges also accept convenience store payments through services like Family Mart, Lawson, and 7-Eleven. You generate a payment number or barcode in the exchange's app, bring it to the store, and pay in cash. Deposits appear in your exchange account within 10 to 60 minutes. Convenience store deposits often carry fees of 300 to 700 yen per transaction and may have daily limits around 300,000 yen. Some platforms support Quick Deposit services from internet banks and Pay-easy transfers through ATMs. Withdrawal fees to your bank account typically range from 200 to 750 yen depending on the exchange and amount.

sections.h: Trading Fees and Spreads
p: FSA-registered exchanges charge fees through maker-taker models or spreads. Maker-taker exchanges like Bitbank and GMO Coin charge separate fees for orders that add liquidity (maker orders, typically 0% to negative 0.02%, meaning you earn a rebate) and orders that remove liquidity (taker orders, typically 0.05% to 0.15%). These exchanges display order books where you can see buy and sell orders at specific prices.

Other platforms like Coincheck use a simpler model where you buy and sell at quoted prices that include a spread—the difference between the buy price and sell price. Spreads vary by cryptocurrency and market conditions but typically range from 0.1% to 5%. Wider spreads mean higher effective costs. When comparing exchanges, calculate the total cost including both trading fees and any deposit or withdrawal charges. Some exchanges waive maker fees or offer reduced rates for high-volume traders.

sections.h: Tax Treatment: Crypto Profits as Miscellaneous Income
p: Japan does not treat cryptocurrency profits as capital gains. Instead, the National Tax Agency classifies them as miscellaneous income (zatsushotoku), subject to progressive income tax rates ranging from 5% to 45% plus local inhabitant tax of approximately 10%. This means your total annual income, including salary and crypto profits, determines your tax rate. For example, if your combined income falls in the 20% bracket, your effective rate including local tax approaches 30%.

You must calculate profit for each cryptocurrency transaction using methods like moving-average cost or total-average cost to determine your acquisition cost. If you trade crypto for another crypto (not just selling for yen), that transaction triggers taxable income. Many exchanges provide annual transaction reports, but you remain responsible for accurate calculation and filing. Losses can offset other miscellaneous income but not employment income or capital gains from stocks. Because tax rules change and calculation can be complex, this is not tax advice; consult a Japanese tax professional (zeirishi) familiar with cryptocurrency, especially if your profits exceed basic deduction amounts or you trade frequently.

sections.h: Choosing an Exchange Based on Your Needs
p: Different exchanges suit different priorities. Bitbank and GMO Coin offer professional trading interfaces with order books, lower fees for active traders, and a wide range of cryptocurrencies. Coincheck provides a simpler interface favored by beginners, faster onboarding, and easy convenience store deposits, though spreads may be higher. DMM Bitcoin specializes in leveraged trading for users interested in margin positions. BitFlyer offers strong security with insurance coverage and handles both simple purchases and advanced trading.

Consider which cryptocurrencies you want to buy, as not all exchanges list the same assets. Check whether the exchange supports your preferred deposit method and whether fees fit your transaction size. Larger purchases often benefit from exchanges with tighter spreads or lower percentage fees, while smaller, infrequent purchases may prioritize convenience and interface simplicity over per-transaction costs. Security features like two-factor authentication, cold wallet storage, and insurance should factor into your decision regardless of trading style.

sections.h: Security and Fund Protection
p: FSA regulations require exchanges to hold customer crypto assets separately from company assets and to maintain a certain level of net assets as financial backing. Most exchanges store the majority of customer funds in cold wallets (offline storage), moving only the necessary amount to hot wallets for daily withdrawals. This reduces risk from hacking. Some exchanges like bitFlyer carry insurance policies covering losses from unauthorized access or security breaches, though coverage terms and limits vary.

Enable two-factor authentication using an authenticator app like Google Authenticator or Authy rather than SMS, which is vulnerable to SIM-swap attacks. Use a strong, unique password and consider using a hardware security key if the exchange supports it. Be aware that while FSA registration reduces risk compared to unregulated platforms, no exchange is immune to security incidents. Never store large amounts on an exchange long-term; transfer significant holdings to a personal hardware wallet where you control the private keys. Phishing attempts often impersonate exchanges, so always type the exchange URL manually or use a bookmark rather than clicking links in emails.

es.title: Cómo comprar criptomonedas en España: proveedores registrados, SEPA, KYC e impuestos
es.excerpt: España aplica la regulación MiCA de la UE y mantiene un registro de proveedores de activos virtuales en el Banco de España. Esta guía cubre la verificación de proveedores, opciones de pago, requisitos de identidad, comisiones y las obligaciones fiscales sobre ganancias y tenencias de criptomonedas.

sections.h: Consulta el registro del Banco de España antes de depositar
p: España exige que los exchanges de criptomonedas y los proveedores de monederos se registren en el Banco de España como proveedores de servicios de monedas virtuales. El registro oficial recoge todos los operadores legales y es de consulta pública en la web del Banco de España. Antes de transferir dinero o facilitar documentos de identidad, verifica que la plataforma elegida aparece en este registro. Operar sin registro es ilegal, y los proveedores no registrados no ofrecen protección legal si pierdes fondos o tu cuenta queda bloqueada.

El registro incluye tanto empresas españolas como plataformas extranjeras autorizadas para operar con residentes en España. Muestra el nombre de la empresa, número de registro y fecha de autorización. La normativa MiCA de la UE, que España aplica, establece estándares comunes entre estados miembros, pero el registro sigue siendo nacional. Si una plataforma afirma operar en España pero no aparece en el registro, evítala sin importar su publicidad o reputación aparente.

sections.h: Depósitos en euros por transferencia SEPA y Bizum
p: La mayoría de los exchanges españoles aceptan transferencias bancarias SEPA para depositar euros. Las transferencias SEPA son gratuitas desde bancos españoles, suelen llegar en un día hábil y no implican conversión de divisa, ya que tanto tu cuenta bancaria como la del exchange están en euros. Debes facilitar el IBAN del exchange, código de referencia y nombre del remitente que coincida con tu cuenta verificada. Las transferencias SEPA inmediatas, admitidas por muchos bancos españoles, pueden acreditar tu saldo en segundos por una comisión pequeña, normalmente inferior a un euro.

Bizum cuenta con soporte creciente en exchanges enfocados al mercado español para depósitos pequeños, con límites que suelen rondar unos cientos de euros por transacción. Las transferencias Bizum son instantáneas y gratuitas para quien envía, aunque el exchange puede aplicar una comisión de conveniencia o reservar este método para usuarios verificados. Para cantidades mayores, SEPA estándar sigue siendo el método dominante. Algunas plataformas también aceptan tarjetas de débito, pero los depósitos con tarjeta suelen conllevar comisiones del 1,5 al 3 por ciento y límites más estrictos por el riesgo de contracargo.

sections.h: Verificación KYC con DNI o NIE
p: Todos los proveedores de criptomonedas registrados en España deben realizar verificación de identidad (Know Your Customer) antes de permitir operaciones o depósitos significativos. Necesitarás aportar un documento de identidad válido emitido por el gobierno: los nacionales españoles usan el Documento Nacional de Identidad (DNI), mientras que los extranjeros residentes facilitan el Número de Identidad de Extranjero (NIE). Algunas plataformas también aceptan pasaportes, pero DNI y NIE son los documentos estándar y se procesan más rápido.

La verificación suele requerir subir una foto o escaneo nítido del documento, un selfie o vídeo en directo para cotejar tu rostro, y un justificante de domicilio reciente como factura de suministros, extracto bancario o certificado de empadronamiento con tu dirección en España. El procesamiento tarda desde unos minutos hasta varios días según la plataforma y el volumen. Puede requerirse una nueva verificación si cambias de domicilio o si las normas regulatorias se endurecen. Hasta que el KYC esté completo, los depósitos y el trading están bloqueados del todo o limitados a cantidades muy bajas.

sections.h: Comisiones de trading, spread y costes de retirada
p: Los exchanges cobran de una o ambas formas: una comisión porcentual en cada compra o venta, y un spread entre el precio de compra y el de venta. Las comisiones de trading en plataformas españolas suelen oscilar entre el 0,1 y el 1 por ciento por operación, a menudo estructuradas en tramos que premian mayor volumen mensual con tarifas más bajas. El spread—la diferencia entre el precio al que el exchange compra y vende una criptomoneda—puede añadir otro 0,5 al 2 por ciento en coste implícito, especialmente en plataformas que anuncian trading sin comisiones.

Retirar euros de vuelta a tu cuenta bancaria suele ser gratuito por SEPA, aunque algunos exchanges establecen un importe mínimo de retirada o cobran una tarifa fija de uno o dos euros. Retirar criptomonedas a un monedero externo conlleva comisiones de red blockchain, que varían según el activo y la congestión de la red. Las retiradas de Bitcoin pueden costar unos pocos euros, mientras que Ethereum o tokens en Ethereum pueden costar bastante más en periodos de alta actividad. Consulta siempre el cuadro de comisiones en la página de tarifas de la plataforma, ya que las promociones caducan y las estructuras cambian.

sections.h: IRPF sobre ganancias de criptomonedas: tramos del ahorro
p: Las ganancias de criptomonedas en España tributan como rendimientos del ahorro y se gravan por separado de los ingresos del trabajo o actividades económicas. El impuesto se aplica solo al vender, intercambiar por otra criptomoneda o usar cripto para comprar bienes o servicios; simplemente mantener no genera hecho imponible. Los rendimientos del ahorro tributan en tramos progresivos: conforme a la ley vigente, los primeros 6.000 € tributan al 19 por ciento, de 6.000 a 50.000 € al 21 por ciento, de 50.000 a 200.000 € al 23 por ciento, y por encima de 200.000 € al 26 por ciento. Estos tramos y tipos los fija el Estado, aunque las comunidades autónomas pueden ajustarlos levemente.

Las pérdidas de operaciones con cripto pueden compensar ganancias dentro del mismo ejercicio fiscal y hasta los cuatro siguientes, pero solo contra otros rendimientos del ahorro como dividendos o intereses, no contra rendimientos del trabajo. Se calcula la ganancia o pérdida por operación usando el coste de adquisición y el precio de venta en euros. Mantener un registro detallado de cada transacción, incluyendo fecha, importe, activo, precio y comisiones, es imprescindible. Las normas y tipos cambian con los presupuestos anuales, y esto no es asesoramiento fiscal: consulta con un asesor fiscal español para garantizar el cumplimiento según tu situación concreta.

sections.h: Modelo 721: declaración de criptomonedas en el extranjero
p: Si mantienes criptomonedas en un exchange extranjero o en monederos no custodiados por un proveedor español, y el valor conjunto supera los 50.000 € en cualquier momento del año natural, debes presentar el modelo 721 (Declaración informativa sobre monedas virtuales situadas en el extranjero) antes del 31 de marzo del año siguiente. El umbral se aplica por persona, no por cuenta o activo, y se mide con el valor máximo alcanzado durante el año convertido a euros al tipo de cambio de esa fecha.

El modelo 721 es una declaración informativa, no un pago de impuestos. Su propósito es la transparencia, permitiendo que la Agencia Tributaria cruce las tenencias con las declaraciones de renta. No presentar, hacerlo fuera de plazo o facilitar información incorrecta puede resultar en sanciones significativas, desde 5.000 € por grupo de activos no declarados y aumentando en caso de reincidencia. Si tus tenencias están por debajo de 50.000 € o están exclusivamente con proveedores registrados en España, el modelo 721 no aplica. Las normas y sanciones pueden cambiar, así que verifica los umbrales y requisitos vigentes cada año o trabaja con un profesional fiscal familiarizado con la declaración de criptomonedas.

en.title: How to Buy Cryptocurrency in Spain: Providers, Payments, KYC, and Taxes
en.excerpt: Spain operates under EU MiCA regulations and maintains a Banco de España registry of authorized virtual asset service providers. This guide covers verifying providers, funding options, identity requirements, fees, and the tax obligations that apply to crypto gains and holdings.

sections.h: Check the Banco de España register before you deposit
p: Spain requires cryptocurrency exchanges and wallet providers to register with the Banco de España as virtual currency service providers. The official register lists every legal operator and is publicly searchable on the Banco de España website. Before transferring money or providing identity documents, verify that your chosen platform appears on this register. Operating without registration is illegal, and unregistered providers offer no legal recourse if funds are lost or frozen.

The register includes both Spanish companies and foreign platforms authorized to serve Spanish residents. It shows the company name, registration number, and the date of authorization. EU MiCA rules, which Spain applies, set common standards across member states, but registration remains national. If a platform claims to serve Spain but does not appear on the register, avoid it regardless of marketing or perceived reputation.

sections.h: EUR deposits via SEPA transfer and Bizum
p: Most Spanish exchanges accept SEPA bank transfers for depositing euros. SEPA transfers are free from Spanish banks, typically arrive within one business day, and involve no currency conversion since both your bank account and the exchange account are denominated in euros. You provide the exchange's IBAN, reference code, and sender name that matches your verified account. Instant SEPA transfers, supported by many Spanish banks, can credit your exchange balance within seconds for a small fee, typically under one euro.

Bizum is increasingly supported by Spanish-focused exchanges for smaller deposits, usually capped at a few hundred euros per transaction. Bizum transfers are instant and free for the sender, though exchanges may apply a convenience fee or reserve this method for verified users. For larger amounts, standard SEPA remains the dominant method. Some platforms also accept debit cards, but card deposits often incur fees of 1.5 to 3 percent and face stricter limits due to chargeback risk.

sections.h: KYC verification with DNI or NIE
p: All registered Spanish crypto providers must perform Know Your Customer verification before allowing trades or significant deposits. You will need to provide a valid government-issued identity document—Spanish nationals use the Documento Nacional de Identidad (DNI), while foreign residents provide the Número de Identidad de Extranjero (NIE). Some platforms also accept passports, but DNI and NIE are standard and process faster.

Verification typically involves uploading a clear photo or scan of your document, a selfie or live video to match your face, and proof of residence such as a recent utility bill, bank statement, or padrón certificate showing your Spanish address. Processing takes anywhere from a few minutes to a few days depending on the platform and volume. Repeat verification may be required if you change address or if regulatory rules tighten. Until KYC is complete, deposits and trading are either blocked entirely or capped at very low amounts.

sections.h: Trading fees, spreads, and withdrawal costs
p: Exchanges charge in one or both of two ways: a percentage trading fee on each buy or sell, and a spread between the buy and sell price. Trading fees on Spanish platforms typically range from 0.1 to 1 percent per transaction, often structured in tiers that reward higher monthly volume with lower rates. The spread—the difference between the price at which the exchange buys and sells a cryptocurrency—can add another 0.5 to 2 percent in implicit cost, especially on platforms that advertise zero-commission trading.

Withdrawing euros back to your bank account is usually free via SEPA, though some exchanges set a minimum withdrawal amount or charge a flat fee of one or two euros. Withdrawing cryptocurrency to an external wallet incurs blockchain network fees, which vary by asset and network congestion. Bitcoin withdrawals might cost a few euros, while Ethereum or tokens on Ethereum can cost significantly more during busy periods. Always confirm the fee schedule in the platform's fee page, as promotional rates expire and structures change.

sections.h: Income tax on crypto gains: savings income bands
p: Cryptocurrency gains in Spain are treated as savings income (rendimientos del ahorro) and taxed separately from employment or business income. The tax applies only when you sell, trade for another cryptocurrency, or use crypto to buy goods or services—simply holding does not trigger a taxable event. Savings income is taxed in progressive bands: as of current law, the first €6,000 is taxed at 19 percent, income from €6,000 to €50,000 at 21 percent, €50,000 to €200,000 at 23 percent, and income above €200,000 at 26 percent. These bands and rates are set by the state, though autonomous communities can adjust them slightly.

Losses from crypto trades can offset gains within the same tax year and up to four subsequent years, but only against other savings income such as dividends or interest, not against employment income. You calculate the gain or loss per transaction using the acquisition cost and the sale price in euros. Keeping detailed records of every transaction, including date, amount, asset, price, and fees, is essential. Rules and rates do change with annual budgets, and this is not tax advice—consult a Spanish tax advisor (asesor fiscal) to ensure compliance with your specific situation.

sections.h: Modelo 721: declaring crypto held abroad
p: If you hold cryptocurrency on a foreign exchange or in wallets not custodied by a Spanish provider, and the combined value exceeds €50,000 at any point during the calendar year, you must file modelo 721 (Declaración informativa sobre monedas virtuales situadas en el extranjero) by March 31 of the following year. The threshold applies per person, not per account or asset, and is measured using the highest value reached during the year converted to euros at the exchange rate of that date.

Modelo 721 is an informational declaration, not a tax payment. Its purpose is transparency, allowing the tax authority (Agencia Tributaria) to cross-reference holdings with income declarations. Failing to file, filing late, or providing incorrect information can result in significant penalties, starting at €5,000 per undeclared asset group and increasing for repeat offenses. If your holdings are below €50,000 or are held exclusively with Spanish-registered providers, modelo 721 does not apply. Rules and penalties are subject to change, so verify current thresholds and requirements each year or work with a tax professional familiar with crypto reporting.

hi.title: भारत में क्रिप्टोकरेंसी कैसे खरीदें: INR जमा, KYC, 30% टैक्स और 1% TDS
